examples: The mouse will nibble the cheese.
Fish nibble at the bread.
I nibble my cracker.

more.def: To eat something by taking small bites.
examples: The rabbit nibbled on a carrot.
Mice had nibbled a hole in the bag of grain.
The goat nibbled at my sleeve.
She is a nice girl.
He was nice to me.
What a nice dog!
The nice neighbor brought us a basket of apples.
We had a nice walk along the beach.
It is nice to see you again.

easy.def: The time when it is dark and people sleep.
examples: The moon shines at night.
Good night!
I sleep all night.

more.def: The time between sunset and sunrise, when it is dark outside.
examples: Owls hunt at night when the forest is quiet.
We camped under the stars all night.
It was a cold night, so we lit the fire.
I had a nightmare.
The nightmare woke me.
A nightmare is a bad dream.

more.def: A frightening dream that happens while you sleep.
examples: I woke up from a nightmare.
The nightmare was about a giant spider.
Dad hugged me after my nightmare.

related.def: Very scary, like a bad dream.

examples: I have nine crayons.
My cat is nine.
There are nine kids.

more.def: The number 9, which comes after eight and before ten.
examples: A baseball team has nine players on the field.
School starts at nine o'clock.
She turned nine last week.
I have nineteen coins.
Nineteen kids came to the party.
He is nineteen.

more.def: The number 19, which comes after eighteen and before twenty.
examples: The nineteen students lined up for the bus.
Nineteen days passed before the seeds sprouted.
She counted nineteen boats on the bay.
